rationale: B wins because it finds the story A leaves half-buried: "Anker says its home battery needs no major rewiring. Installers will decide if that's true." That is a real trade piece with a protagonist, a falsifiable claim, and the possibility the story turns against the company. A has good bones, but "The phone-charger company now wants to power your whole house" leans into a category thesis it admits still needs "any second consumer-electronics maker." Fine instinct, but not the sharpest blade in the drawer.
gaps_in_A: "A profitable public electronics giant is funding its own move into home energy" overreaches. Profitable and public does not prove Anker is self-funding this line or taking the liabilities onto its own balance sheet.

"consumer-electronics brands move into whole-home energy" is premature trend packaging. The set itself admits it needs "any second consumer-electronics maker," which means the angle is currently a single-company entrant story, not category creation.

"Anker is betting it can take on Tesla Powerwall without the rewiring" jams two stories together: Powerwall competition and installation-verification. The stronger journalist-shaped angle is installers testing the rewiring claim.

"newsjack-detector — none of these angles is anchored to a current external signal" overcorrects. The US launch is a legitimate trade peg; the immediate gating items are pricing, capacity, warranty, and installer proof.
gaps_in_B: "purchase costing thousands of dollars and living on the side of the house for a decade" smuggles in price and lifetime color not supplied in the update. Plausible is not the same as grounded.

"The prevailing belief is that whole-home batteries mean panel work, transfer switches, and an electrician's week" needs sourcing. Without external evidence, that setup line is a confident assumption wearing a hard hat.
"it has never carried at this scale" is directionally sensible but not directly in the facts. Label it as the question reporters should test, not a proven company history claim.
